data.name: Harrie
data.gender_notes: Harrie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Germanic words ‘har’ meaning army and ‘ric’ meaning ruler or power. The name Harrie is derived from the old English word ‘hereweard’ meaning army brave or army ruler. The name Harrie carries the meaning “Free, Bright” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Harrie usually hope their child will grow to embody free, bright and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes bravery, leadership, and strength in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Harrie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, Bright.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harrie total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Harrie, as a Germanic name, carries the strength and courage associated with the meanings of its roots. It resonates with individuals who value leadership, integrity, and a sense of duty or service. This name may have been popular among warriors and soldiers throughout history, reflecting the warrior spirit and sense of protection it embodies.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Harrie can be seen as a reminder of the power and protection that comes from God, our ultimate ruler and protector. The name may inspire individuals to adopt a strong and courageous spirit in their own faith, drawing on inner strength and resilience in the face of challenges. Additionally, the name can serve as a reminder of the church as a collective army, united in their commitment to the teachings of Christ, and courageously spreading His message in the world.
